compiledFrom: Read-only research of 5 public repositories (source, issues, commits, web reports). Ratings describe evidence, not truth.

ratingScale.A: Independently verified with tests or artifacts
ratingScale.B: Code and methodology present, no independent verification
ratingScale.C: Claims in README only, weak substantiation

principles: Outcome ratings concern the claimed effect on TikTok processing, not whether the code produces a valid MP4.
No method in this database has any rating above B for outcome. Nothing is verified end to end.
Every engine in this tool is evaluated by local structural validation only. Output is labeled LOCAL VALIDATION, never a platform verdict.
The original file is never modified. SHA-256 of the source is checked before and after; a mismatch disables download.
Fragmented (fMP4) inputs are normalized to progressive MP4 before any engine runs; engines classify fragmented input as unsupported.
localTestStatus reflects actual local gate runs recorded by this project's test suite; liveTestStatus is updated only by a performed live upload test.

methods.name: Sample-table ghost frames
methods.description: Inflate stts/stsz/stsc/stco with fake samples (typically x10) pointing at one small filler NAL, so the file declares a much higher frame density. mdat real samples are untouched.
knownLimitations: Header durations and timestamps exclude the padding samples, so tools that count samples rather than read headers see a different frame count.
The shared filler NAL is intentionally not decodable; tools that decode every sample report errors in the padding region.
methods.knownTikTokEvidence: Adverse user reports only: upload stuck 'under review' (tiktok-quality issue #1), forced-private/takedown reports (NoBlur issues #2-#4), one 'didnt work' report (tiktok-lossless-upload issue #1). No verified positive outcome anywhere.

facts: 13-step pure container rewrite in src/tiktok_quality/transform.py; no pixel changes; MIT; single commit 5fc3907 (2026-06-16).
Tests are builder/parser round-trips only; proof.png is one self-produced checker screenshot with no A/B baseline.
Issue #1 (2026-09-23, unanswered): upload stuck 'under review' more than 48h.
PR #2 (2026-09-25): 'improved randomization for frames so tiktok aint detecting shi' implies the deterministic pattern is a detection signal.
Known gaps: stco only (no co64), H.264 only, unguarded audio elst, version-0 box assumptions.
Client-side Vite JS app; codec-aware dummy sizes (H.264 8B, HEVC 16B, VP9/AV1 4B); co64 support; moov-before-mdat with chunk-offset fixup.
Owner in issue #1 (2026-06-06): 'the patch doesn't work anymore because a new TikTok update blocks it'.
Blocking issues #2 (2026-08-05), #3 (2026-08-10), #4 (2026-08-15): patched videos forced private or taken down.
No license file (all rights reserved); last push 2026-07-29, no fix shipped after reports.
Optional VFI mode re-encodes (libx264 CRF20 ultrafast): quality loss, banned in this tool.
Python patcher inflates a duplicated audio track's sample tables (avc1 8B, hvc1 16B, vp09/av01 4B table credited to NoBlur).
Default CLI path re-encodes (libx264 CRF18); a remux path exists but is not the default.
Issue #1 (2026-08-11, 'didnt work'): sole user report says quality was still bad; closed without diagnosis.
Shipped a broken chunk-offset traversal (matched 'media' instead of 'mdia') for roughly 8 weeks; outputs before 2026-10-05 are suspect.
Tests were added in PR #2 then deleted on merge (2026-10-05); no CI.

portNotes: Filler target: append one dedicated 8-byte NAL (00 00 00 04 00 00 00 00) at end of mdat and point all ghost offsets there (tiktok-quality approach), not at real media bytes.
Support co64, versioned boxes, and non-H.264 codecs or gate them as ineligible; never scan payload bytes for box markers.
Randomized filler sizes and jittered deltas (tiktok-quality PR #2 idea) reduce deterministic fingerprints; keep detectability heuristics (stco uniqueness, size entropy) as local signals only.

methods.name: Timescale division in mvhd/mdhd
methods.description: Divide movie/track timescale and duration by a divider (60fps: 2, 120fps: 4) while leaving stts deltas untouched, so the file declares a lower frame rate to the server but keeps every frame.
knownLimitations: This port divides only the video track's mdhd timescale and duration; audio, mvhd and tkhd stay untouched (reference tools divide mvhd too, some without adjusting tkhd, which desynchronizes header durations).

stts deltas are untouched, so sample timestamps stretch by the divider while the header duration stays the same; local players may present fewer frames or run slower than the source. Timing change is declared to the user.
Eligibility requires an exactly divisible video timescale and duration and a declared 60fps or 120fps; other frame rates are refused.
methods.knownTikTokEvidence: README claims only, contradicted internally (README says timescale is inflated, code divides it). The primary source's own research doc states no local MP4 method was found to work 100% after server processing. One unanswered report of mobile glitches after patching.

facts: C++/Qt app; patches mvhd and every mdhd timescale and duration by division; mdat and sample tables never touched.
README says timescale is inflated; code divides it (README contradicts itself).
Patches audio mdhd too (48000 divided), risking desync; naive indexOf('mvhd') byte scan can hit payload; mvhd version-1 offset bug.
Issue #2 (2026-05-01, unanswered): still glitchy on mobile after patch, contradicting the README mitigation claim.
License file says GPL-3.0 while README claims MIT; treat as GPL-3.0.
Browser JS patcher with three methods; balanced-sync divides mvhd and video mdhd timescale/duration then adds an elst with media_rate = divider; classic-force replicates ut0ku without elst.
Synthetic box tests only (4-96 byte fake boxes); no real fixtures, no CI, issues disabled.

Own research doc (docs/tiktok-method-research.md, 2026-06-11): 'Current research did not find any additional local MP4 method that works 100% after TikTok server processing' and 'Do not claim Upload120 bypasses TikTok compression'.
Adds u120 and iTunes tags that fingerprint the output as produced by this tool.

portNotes: Only edit the video track's mdhd; never divide audio timescale.
Walk the parsed box tree; never indexOf-scan raw bytes.
Declared timing becomes internally inconsistent with stts; treat as an explicit, documented candidate with local playback warnings, not a default.

methods.name: Edit-list media rate signaling
methods.description: Insert an edts/elst with media_rate integer set (1.0x as identity signal, or N.0x after a timescale division) plus marker tags in udta/meta.
knownLimitations: Inserts the identity edit list only when the video track has no edit list; files that already carry one are refused rather than modified.
Marker tags and 'Patched by' strings from reference tools are deliberately not reproduced.
methods.knownTikTokEvidence: No outcome measurements in either source; issues disabled on the primary repo; no community signal exists. One source credits a commercial browser extension without data.

facts: extension-signal method inserts identity elst (media_rate 1/1) plus 'TikTok Web Signal' tags with no timing change at all.
No outcome measurements anywhere in the repo; issues are disabled so no community signal exists.
Rebases stco/co64 correctly on box insertion (applyOperations) with checkedU32 overflow guards.
v1 (Aug 2026) inflated elst from 0x1 to 0x10000001, credited to a commercial browser extension; superseded by the current pipeline.
Identity elst insert remains in the current patcher.

portNotes: elst insertion is spec-legal and quality-neutral; platform effect unknown (self-reported only).
Marker tags and 'Patched by' strings are fingerprints; this tool adds none.

methods.name: Container hygiene remux
methods.description: Non-semantic normalization: moov before mdat (fast-start), ftyp brand normalize, strip timestamps and identifying metadata, remove udta junk, unify handler names. No claim of affecting platform processing.
knownLimitations: May realign audio edit-list timing when the source requires it (reported as stats.audioAdjusted).
Non-AV tracks (timecode, subtitles, metadata tracks) are removed from the output.
methods.knownTikTokEvidence: No source claims this changes platform outcomes; no adverse reports exist because no outcome is claimed.

facts: ftyp mp42 to isom, free box insert, moov-before-mdat with stco recompute, udta/meta rebuild, audio handler rename to SoundHandler.
Metadata scrubbing is standard hygiene; no repo claims it changes platform outcomes on its own.
Creation-time zeroing and handler normalization are documented as hygiene, not as a bypass.

portNotes: This is the only family with no negative reports: it changes no media bytes and makes no promises.
All outputs from this tool are sample-table and header edits over byte-identical mdat payloads; validation asserts that equality directly.

methods.name: Client-side re-encode variants
methods.description: Re-encode video (ffmpeg.wasm or similar) with CRF settings before patching, sometimes spoofing bitrate boxes afterward.
knownLimitations: BANNED in this tool by product rule: video quality is never touched, no exceptions. Documented only.
methods.knownTikTokEvidence: Adverse: sources admit quality loss (CRF 18-20, ultrafast); one source spoofs codec/bitrate boxes and writes an invalid mp4a sample rate.

facts: VFI mode: minterpolate to 60fps with libx264 CRF20 preset ultrafast; README admits speed over quality.
Default encode libx264 CRF18; spoofs avcC/btrt/esds from the source and writes 0 into the mp4a sample-rate field (invalid).

portNotes: BANNED in this tool by product rule: video quality is never touched, no exceptions. Kept in the database only so the ban is documented with evidence.
